paragraphs: SkySafe sells a drone detection and airspace intelligence platform that gives businesses the visibility and forensic detail to identify drone activity in real time and build legally sound cases when incidents occur. The company states the platform detects 96% of drone models, including drones flying without active signals. It can pinpoint where a drone took off, where it landed and the location of its controller. Alerts go out through SMS, Microsoft Teams, Slack, CommandCentral Aware or an existing ops stack. The platform produces forensic reports intended for law enforcement or federal agencies.

One case study describes how a near-miss drone flight over a crowd of 10,000 at Fort Adams State Park led Rhode Island toward a statewide drone detection strategy. The University of Illinois Police Department used SkySafe to monitor and respond to drone activity across campus events and facilities, and the University of Louisiana at Monroe uses it to separate authorized university flights from unauthorized activity.

Press releases on its site describe the product as a cloud-based SaaS platform providing real-time and historical drone data to help distinguish unauthorized drones from authorized ones. In November 2025 it launched Forensics as a Service, which the company says lets agencies and organizations respond to and investigate drone incidents on their own. CEO Grant Jordan served as an officer in the US Air Force for four years after graduating from MIT and was President of Somerset Recon.

quote.text: Airspace is changing, even in the most secure environments. SkySafe enables you to detect, analyze, and act on every drone in your airspace.
